01

The basics

Exactly as you want it printed on the site, not as it appears on your LLC paperwork. If people call you Dave's, we say Dave's.

02

What you want it to do

Not what you want it to look like. If we get this right, the look follows.

03

Your work

This is the one that decides how fast your site goes live, and it is the one everybody gets stuck on. So read the box first.

Do not go take new photos

You already have what I need. Every trade has hundreds of job photos on their phone, taken for insurance or to show a customer. They are sideways, badly lit and full of duplicates, and you think they are unusable.

Most of them are. Forty of them are not, and forty is a whole website. I straighten, crop, colour-correct and caption them. That is my job, not yours.

Share the album, or text me a batch. Ninety seconds of your time instead of a Saturday you were never going to spend.

  • Finished work, wide enough to see the whole thing
  • Before and after pairs, if you have any. These are the most valuable photos you own
  • Your truck, your crew, your shop. People hire people
  • Anything with you in it. Owners photos outperform stock every time
04

What you sell

List them the way you would say them out loud. I will handle the wording. If pricing varies too much to publish, say so and we will put ranges or nothing at all.

05

Questions you answer every day

The ones you are sick of repeating on the phone. These become your FAQ page and they train the assistant that answers at 8pm, so the more you write here the fewer calls you take after hours.

06

Who else is out there

I am going to look anyway. Faster if you tell me, and it is useful to know who you would hate to lose a job to.

07

Practical bits

Loose ends. Say "no" or "not sure" freely, none of these block anything.

08

Send it back

Copy your answers and paste them into an email or a text. Nothing here is submitted automatically, so nothing leaves this page until you send it.

Then send to boyd@rubyxqube.com or text (208) 970-8624. Photos can come separately, whenever they are ready.
